dialog.body: Public Works storm line, this is Kevin.
Hi Kevin, yeah, good afternoon. I know it's Saturday and City Hall's closed up, so I figured this was the line to try. Is this the right one for storm stuff?
You got it. This is the one for storm problems on the weekend. What's going on?

Well, it's the nor'easter, the one that's hitting today. It's been coming down since early this morning and the water is just sitting at the corner. Across the crosswalk by the school bus stop, it's pooled right across the whole thing.
Okay. Where are you calling from, what's the address or the closest one?
I'm at 248 Broadway, up in the North End. The crosswalk is right out front, pretty much.
Got it, 248 Broadway. And the water's across the crosswalk, so deep enough that people can't walk through it?

Deep enough that nobody wants to. And that's the problem, the kids are stepping out into the road to get around it. They're waiting for the bus and they don't want wet sneakers, so they go out around the puddle right into the lane. Cars are coming through, throwing water. I've been at the window watching and I'm not happy about it.
Yeah, that's not good. Are these little kids or older ones?
Mixed. Some of them are grade school age, a couple of bigger ones. Saturday, so I don't know where they're all headed, but there's a bunch.
Okay, I'm writing this down. Water pooled across crosswalk at the bus stop, kids walking into the roadway. Is the drain there blocked, do you think? Can you see a grate?

There's a grate, but it's got leaves and who knows what plastered over it. And this isn't new, Kevin. Every time we get a real rain, same thing. It's the same spot. I've called about it before and nothing gets done.
I hear you. I'll note that it's a repeat location. Anything else you can see out there?

Yeah, there's one more thing. There's a manhole cover a little ways down from the crosswalk, and it looks off to me. Sitting up or kind of crooked, by about an inch, I'd say. Cars hit it and it clunks.
An inch off, so it's raised or not seated flat?
Raised on one side. It's not flush. With all that water around it, somebody's going to hit it and not see it, or a kid's going to trip on it.
Okay. I'll put that in as its own item so it gets looked at separately. Is it in the road or the sidewalk?
In the road, near the curb. Same side as the bus stop.

Good. Same side as the stop, near the curb. [pause] Let me read it back. Two forty-eight Broadway, drain at the crosswalk covered and water pooling, kids stepping into traffic, plus a manhole cover sitting about an inch high near the curb. That right?
That's it exactly. Now, what I want to know is, are you opening a work order on this? And for what date? Because I'd like to hear a day, not just a we'll look into it.

Yes, I'm opening a work order now, two actually, one for the drain and one for the manhole cover. As for the date, during a storm like this the crews go to the emergency stuff first, flooded roads, downed lines. The drain with kids near the road I'm flagging as a safety item, so it should get seen sooner. Realistically I'd say once the storm clears, probably Monday or Tuesday for the crew to get out there.
Monday or Tuesday. Okay. That's the first real answer I've gotten on it. The last time somebody told me they'd put it on a list, and the list must be long.
It's a long list after a storm, no question. But this one's going in with the safety flag, and with the history you're telling me about.

Fine, I appreciate that. You know, my neighbor next door, she's a retired teacher, and she'd tell me it's not a work order for what date, it's a work order for which date. She corrects my grammar every chance she gets. Over the fence, in the driveway, doesn't matter.
Well, I'll put down the date either way. Do you want a call back when it's been scheduled? I've got your phone as the number you're calling from, or do you want to give me a different one?
Use this one, it's 401-555-0186. I'm on the cell, so if I miss it, leave a message.
Zero one eight six, got it. And it's Mr.?
Okafor. Daniel Okafor. O-K-A-F-O-R.
Okafor, thanks. Mr. Okafor, in the meantime, if the water starts coming up over the curb or anyone's in real danger, call 911, don't wait on us.
I will. I just hope somebody comes before one of those kids ends up under a car. That's what's got me worked up. It's the same corner every time and every time I'm the one calling.
Understood. It's logged, with the safety flag. You should hear something from us early in the week.
All right, Kevin. Thanks for picking up on a Saturday. Stay dry down there.
You too, Mr. Okafor. Take care.
